name: Pithom
title: Egyptian Store City
summary: Pithom (also spelled Pitom) was one of the two store cities that the Israelites were forced to build during their slavery in Egypt. Although Pithom is not a person but a city, it is mentioned in the Bible in connection with the oppression of the people of Israel under Pharaoh. The city is an important symbol of the suffering the Israelites endured before their deliverance from Egypt.

keyEvents.title: Building Store Cities During Slavery
keyEvents.description: The Israelites were put to forced labor and had to build the store cities Pithom and Rameses for Pharaoh. This was part of the systematic oppression of the Israelite people in Egypt.

keyEvents.title: Pharaoh's Oppression of the Israelites
keyEvents.description: Pharaoh feared the growing Israelite population and imposed hard forced labor on them, including the construction of Pithom. This oppression became part of the background for God's call to Moses.

keyEvents.title: Israel's Cry to God
keyEvents.description: During the harsh slavery, which included the work of building Pithom, the Israelites cried out to God for help, and God heard their cry.

keyEvents.title: God's Promise of Deliverance
keyEvents.description: God revealed Himself to Moses in the burning bush and promised to deliver the Israelites from the oppression they suffered in Egypt, where the construction of Pithom was a central part of their slavery.

keyEvents.title: The Exodus from Egypt
keyEvents.description: After the plagues upon Egypt, the Israelites were finally freed from slavery, which included forced labor building store cities like Pithom.
